title: A targeted BattlEye module in 2020: driver files, windows and memory
summary: The March 2020 researcher-described module covered substantially more than a normal executable-memory report. The article’s host comparison suggests selective delivery, while the window-title pseudocode notably complicates the accompanying privacy prose.
author: Observatory editorial
takeaways: A negative observation on another machine does not reveal BattlEye’s targeting criterion or its rollout rate.
The decompiled driver upload branch is filename-pattern-limited; do not describe bulk uploading of all drivers.
The article’s own window loop masks title bytes before transmission, despite prose implying raw title transmission.
Collection and a send function do not disclose backend retention, decisions or appeal policy.

sections.title: Why the researcher thought delivery was selective
Memory signals are not enforcement decisions
